voltage.definition: The electrical force that pushes electric charges through a circuit, similar to pressure pushing water through a pipe.

current.definition: The flow of electric charge through a wire or circuit.

electric charge.definition: A property of matter that causes it to experience a force in an electric field, either positive or negative.

circuit.definition: A complete path that allows electric current to flow.

circuits.definition: A complete path that allows electric current to flow.

ammeter.definition: A device used to measure electric current.

voltmeter.definition: A device used to measure electrical voltage.

electrons.definition: Tiny negatively charged particles that move through materials to create electricity.

conductor.definition: A material that allows electric current to flow easily through it.

electrolytes.definition: Liquids or substances that conduct electricity because they contain charged particles.

potential difference.definition: Another name for voltage; the difference in electrical energy between two points.

magnetic field.definition: An invisible area around a magnet or electric current where magnetic forces act.

electromagnetism.definition: The relationship between electricity and magnetism, where electric currents create magnetic fields.

electromagnetic induction.definition: The process of generating electric current by changing a magnetic field near a wire.

coil.definition: A wire wound in loops that strengthens magnetic and electrical effects.

generator.definition: A machine that converts motion into electrical energy.

alternator.definition: A type of generator that produces alternating current (AC).

alternating current.definition: Electric current that regularly changes direction, like the electricity used in homes.

direct current.definition: Electric current that flows in one direction only, like electricity from a battery.

capacitor.definition: A component that stores electrical energy for a short time.

rectifier.definition: A device that converts alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC).

frequency.definition: How often an electric signal or wave repeats each second, measured in hertz (Hz).

static electricity.definition: Electric charge that builds up on an object and does not flow until discharged.

discharge.definition: The sudden release of stored electric energy.

ionization.definition: The process where atoms gain or lose electrons, allowing electricity to flow through air.

arc.definition: A bright electrical discharge traveling through air between two conductors.

antenna.definition: A device that sends or receives electromagnetic waves.

electromagnetic waves.definition: Waves of energy that travel through space at the speed of light, including radio waves and light.

radio waves.definition: A type of electromagnetic wave used to transmit information wirelessly.

bandwidth.definition: The amount of information that can be transmitted over a signal.

polarization.definition: The direction in which an electromagnetic wave vibrates.

microwaves.definition: Electromagnetic waves used for cooking, communication, and radar.

electromagnetic spectrum.definition: The full range of electromagnetic waves, from radio waves to gamma rays.

infrared.definition: Electromagnetic waves associated with heat and used in night vision and remote controls.

ultraviolet.definition: High-energy electromagnetic waves that can sterilize surfaces but also harm skin.

x-rays.definition: High-energy electromagnetic waves used to see inside objects, such as in medical imaging.

gamma rays.definition: The most energetic electromagnetic waves, produced by radioactive materials and cosmic events.

capacitance.definition: The ability of a system to store electric charge.
